grant_statement: Adds a second way to start Qoder CLI: a button that starts it in ACP mode. KalaReach types one line into your shell (it begins with `kr-hook acp`) and Qoder CLI then runs from a private copy of its program file that KalaReach checked against a signed record. KalaReach is its only client. Qoder CLI has no terminal of its own in this mode: you cannot type to it, and its menus and sign-in screens do not appear. You read and answer its approvals in KalaReach. Qoder CLI runs from the same kind of checked private copy. There is no private settings folder: it signs in by itself from the token in its own environment variable or from the sign-in it already holds, it may refresh that sign-in and write its own history, and it starts the MCP servers its own settings name. Test turns may be charged to that account. Its question tool is switched off in this mode. The variables KalaReach copies and sets are listed in the host's reading below. Those are the only variables that KalaReach copies from your shell into Qoder CLI's start. Qoder CLI starts without your language settings, so it starts in the C locale; it, its settings and its hooks add names of their own to the programs they start (Qoder CLI adds `GIT_EDITOR` to its commands and may use a login shell), and KalaReach promises only what it copies. Its own settings, hooks and permission rules apply, so it may act without asking, and KalaReach shows a warning when it reports a mode that allows that. KalaReach checks Qoder CLI's file whole before the start and the running process once after it, so a change by another program of yours between the two is detected after the process starts, and KalaReach then ends it; the replaced file has by then run with your environment. The second limit above (the `kr-hook` file) applies too. On macOS, and on Linux where no session control group exists, KalaReach starts Qoder CLI only when the host configuration records `reduced` ownership for this package (the entry rule of the Gemini text applies: an offer to write it only where the package has none, and no start and no change where it says `full`), and the process-tracking limit of the Gemini text applies. "Cancel" asks Qoder CLI to stop the running turn, also a turn that Qoder CLI began on its own, and removes every message waiting in KalaReach's line. It can lose: Qoder CLI may finish first, and a turn it began on its own may keep acting, because KalaReach cannot know when such a turn ends. For 30 seconds after a Cancel, or until KalaReach sends your next message to Qoder CLI, whichever comes first, KalaReach declines each approval request that arrives, with a notice. From the moment KalaReach sends your next message, every approval request shows as usual, whichever turn it belongs to, and it can belong to the old turn if Qoder CLI has not finished it. KalaReach cannot make Qoder CLI stop acting.
